notes: Scholarly translator endnotes (1-47) by Rev. Lal Behari Day (1883), preserved separately from narrative folktale passages.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Kings, in Bengali folk-tales, have invariably two queens--the elder is called duo, that is, not loved; and the younger is called suo, that is, loved.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Dalim or dadimba means a pomegranate, and kumara son.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Bidhata-Purusha is the deity that predetermines all the events of the life of man or woman, and writes on the forehead of the child, on the sixth day of its birth, a brief precis of them.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: There are eight forms of marriage spoken of in the Hindu Sastras, of which the Gandharva is one, consisting in the exchange of garlands.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Alakta is leaves or flimsy paper saturated with lac.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: A sort of open Palki, used generally for carrying the bridegroom and bride in marriage processions.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Handi is an earthen pot, generally used in cooking food.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Mudki, fried paddy boiled dry in treacle or sugar.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: A sort of sweetmeat made of curds and sugar.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Rakshasas and Rakshasis (male and female) are in Hindu mythology huge giants and giantesses, or rather demons. The word means literally raw-eaters; they were probably the chiefs of the aborigines whom the Aryans overthrew on their first settlement in the country.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Dasi is a general name for all maid-servants.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Sphatika is crystal, and sthambha pillar.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Bathing-place, either in a tank or on the bank of a river, generally furnished with flights of steps.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Professional match-makers.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Manik, or rather manikya, is a fabulous precious stone of incredible value. It is found on the head of some species of snakes, and is equal in value to the wealth of seven kings.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Venus, the Morning Star.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: The seat on the back of an elephant.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Sri is another name of Lakshmi, and batsa means child; so that Sribatsa is literally the "child of fortune."

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Shells used as money, one hundred and sixty of which could have been got a few years ago for one pice.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Fried paddy.

annotations.text: This story is not my own. It was recited to me by a story-teller of the other sex who rejoices in the nom de plume "An Inmate of the Calcutta Lunatic Asylum."

annotations.text: The tutelary goddess of a king's household.

annotations.text: A vessel, made generally of brass, for keeping the pan leaf together with betel-nut and other spices.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: A towel used in bathing.

annotations.text: A sort of bed made of rope, supported by posts of wood.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: The sacred basil.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Zenana is not the name of a province in India, as the good people of Scotland the other day took it to be, but the innermost department of a Hindu or Mohammedan house which the women occupy.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: A religious mendicant.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Sankchinnis or Sankhachurnis are female ghosts of white complexion. They usually stand at the dead of night at the foot of trees, and look like sheets of white cloth.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: An exorcist, one who drives away ghosts from possessed persons.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: The ghost of a Brahman who dies unmarried.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: A bigha is about the third part of an acre.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: The chariot of Kuvera, the Hindu god of riches.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: "Hiraman (from harit, green, and mani, a gem), the name of a beautiful species of parrot, a native of the Molucca Islands (Psittacus sinensis)."--Carey's Dictionary of the Bengalee Language, vol. ii. part iii. p. 1537.

annotations.author: Rev. Lal Behari Day
annotations.text: Winged horse, literally, the king of birds.
